focus_area_title: Bridge Communication Between Senior Leaders and Your Team
content_text_body:
Employees who have access to key decision makers tend to trust their company more. The goal is to bridge communication between your team and senior leaders so that everyone understands each other better.

 

 

 

 ### Collect and share stories

 

 Look for examples of leaders' actions that show their personal side and convey the right company values. 

 

 

 

 Do the same with your team. Capture stories where the team has overcome big challenges, worked together to pull off the impossible, and learned or built confidence from failures.

 

 

 

 Share positive stories about senior leaders with your team and vice versa. This will help each group understand the other and feel a sense of shared success.

 

 

 

 ### Be an Effective Advocate

 

 To be an advocate for your team, you must understand each team member's experiences and needs and seek out the appropriate support for them. 

 

 

 

 Practice asking your team members how they are doing, if they need any support, and what concerns they have about their work or the business. 

 

 

 

 Ask them to help you build a case for implementing a new idea, solving a significant problem, or if necessary, gaining more resources.

 

 

 

 Make a commitment to them to share their concerns, ideas, and experiences with senior leaders. Be specific about when and how you will do that, and how you will keep them informed. And be clear and concise about when and why you chose not to pursue a particular request.
